def sum_array (arr: []i64) : i64 =
  reduce (+) 0i64 arr

def map_add (arr: []i64) (value: i64) : []i64 =
  map (\x -> x + value) arr

def map_multiply (arr: []i64) (factor: i64) : []i64 =
  map (\x -> x * factor) arr

def filter_positive (arr: []i64) : []i64 =
  filter (\x -> x > 0i64) arr

def dot_product [n] (a: [n]i64) (b: [n]i64) : i64 =
  reduce (+) 0i64 (map2 (*) a b)

def vector_add [n] (a: [n]i64) (b: [n]i64) : [n]i64 =
  map2 (+) a b

def vector_sub [n] (a: [n]i64) (b: [n]i64) : [n]i64 =
  map2 (-) a b

def vector_scale (arr: []i64) (scalar: i64) : []i64 =
  map (\x -> x * scalar) arr

def find_max (arr: []i64) : i64 =
  reduce i64.max i64.lowest arr

def find_min (arr: []i64) : i64 =
  reduce i64.min i64.highest arr

def count_positive (arr: []i64) : i64 =
  reduce (+) 0i64 (map (\x -> if x > 0i64 then 1i64 else 0i64) arr)

def sum_matrix (mat: [][]i64) : i64 =
  reduce (+) 0i64 (map (\row -> reduce (+) 0i64 row) mat)

def map_matrix (mat: [][]i64) (value: i64) : [][]i64 =
  map (\row -> map (\x -> x + value) row) mat

def matrix_transpose [n][m] (mat: [n][m]i64) : [m][n]i64 =
  transpose mat

def matrix_multiply [m][n][p] (a: [m][n]i64) (b: [n][p]i64) : [m][p]i64 =
  let bt = transpose b
  in map (\ar ->
    map (\bc ->
      reduce (+) 0i64 (map2 (*) ar bc)
    ) bt
  ) a

def prefix_sum (arr: []i64) : []i64 =
  scan (+) 0i64 arr

def scatter_array (dest: []i64) (indices: []i64) (values: []i64) : []i64 =
  let n = length dest
  let m = if length indices < length values then length indices else length values
  in loop acc = copy dest for i < m do
       let idx = indices[i]
       in if idx >= 0i64 && idx < n
          then acc with [idx] = values[i]
          else acc

def gather (src: []i64) (indices: []i64) : []i64 =
  let n = length src
  in map (\i -> if i >= 0i64 && i < n then src[i] else 0i64) indices

def partition_array (arr: []i64) (pivot: i64) : ([]i64, []i64) =
  let left = filter (\x -> x <= pivot) arr
  let right = filter (\x -> x > pivot) arr
  in (left, right)

def histogram (arr: []i64) (num_bins: i64) : []i64 =
  if num_bins <= 0i64 || length arr == 0i64
  then []
  else
    let min_val = find_min arr
    let max_val = find_max arr
    let range = max_val - min_val
    in if range == 0i64
       then
         let result = replicate num_bins 0i64
         in result with [0] = i64.i64 (length arr)
       else
         let bin_size = (range + num_bins - 1i64) / num_bins
         in loop acc = replicate num_bins 0i64 for x in arr do
              let raw_bin = (x - min_val) / bin_size
              let clamped_bin =
                if raw_bin < 0i64 then 0i64
                else if raw_bin >= num_bins then num_bins - 1i64
                else raw_bin
              in acc with [clamped_bin] = acc[clamped_bin] + 1i64

  flatten mat

def flatten_3d (arr: [][][]i64) : []i64 =
  flatten (flatten arr)

def zip_arrays [n] (a: [n]i64) (b: [n]i64) : [n](i64, i64) =
  zip a b

def all_equal (arr: []i64) : bool =

  then true
  else
    let first = arr[0]

def any_positive (arr: []i64) : bool =

def all_positive (arr: []i64) : bool =
  reduce (&&) true (map (\x -> x > 0i64) arr)

def replicate_array (n: i64) (value: i64) : []i64 =
  if n <= 0i64
  then []
  else replicate n value

def iota_array (n: i64) : []i64 =
  if n <= 0i64
  then []
  else iota n

  then arr

     then mat
     else
       let col_count = length mat[row]
       in if col < 0i64 || col >= col_count
          then mat

def mean_array (arr: []f64) : f64 =

     then 0.0
     else reduce (+) 0.0 arr / f64.i64 n

def variance_array (arr: []f64) : f64 =
  let n = length arr
  in if n == 0i64
     then 0.0
     else
       let mean = mean_array arr
       in reduce (+) 0.0 (map (\x -> (x - mean) * (x - mean)) arr) / f64.i64 n

def std_dev_array (arr: []f64) : f64 =
  f64.sqrt (variance_array arr)

def normalize_array (arr: []f64) : []f64 =
  let n = length arr
  in if n == 0i64
     then []
     else
       let mean = mean_array arr
       let std = std_dev_array arr
       in if std == 0.0
          then map (\_ -> 0.0) arr
          else map (\x -> (x - mean) / std) arr

def min_max_normalize (arr: []f64) : []f64 =
  let n = length arr
  in if n == 0i64
     then []
     else
       let min_val = reduce f64.min f64.highest arr
       let max_val = reduce f64.max f64.lowest arr
       let range = max_val - min_val
       in if range == 0.0
          then map (\_ -> 0.0) arr
          else map (\x -> (x - min_val) / range) arr

def euclidean_distance [n] (a: [n]f64) (b: [n]f64) : f64 =
  f64.sqrt (reduce (+) 0.0 (map (\x -> x * x) (map2 (-) a b)))

def cosine_similarity [n] (a: [n]f64) (b: [n]f64) : f64 =
  let dot = reduce (+) 0.0 (map2 (*) a b)
  let mag_a = f64.sqrt (reduce (+) 0.0 (map (\x -> x * x) a))
  let mag_b = f64.sqrt (reduce (+) 0.0 (map (\x -> x * x) b))
  let denom = mag_a * mag_b
  in if denom == 0.0
     then 0.0
     else dot / denom

def softmax (arr: []f64) : []f64 =
  if length arr == 0i64
  then []
  else
    let max_val = reduce f64.max f64.lowest arr
    let exp_vals = map (\x -> f64.exp (x - max_val)) arr
    let sum_exp = reduce (+) 0.0 exp_vals
    in if sum_exp == 0.0
       then map (\_ -> 0.0) exp_vals
       else map (\x -> x / sum_exp) exp_vals

def relu (arr: []f64) : []f64 =
  map (\x -> if x > 0.0 then x else 0.0) arr

def sigmoid (arr: []f64) : []f64 =
  map (\x ->
    if x >= 0.0
    then 1.0 / (1.0 + f64.exp (-x))
    else
      let e = f64.exp x
      in e / (1.0 + e)
  ) arr

def tanh_array (arr: []f64) : []f64 =
  map f64.tanh arr

def leaky_relu (arr: []f64) (alpha: f64) : []f64 =
  map (\x -> if x > 0.0 then x else alpha * x) arr

def elu (arr: []f64) (alpha: f64) : []f64 =
  map (\x -> if x > 0.0 then x else alpha * (f64.exp x - 1.0)) arr

def convolve_1d (signal: []f64) (kernel: []f64) : []f64 =
  let n = length signal
  let k = length kernel
  in if k == 0i64 || k > n
     then []
     else
       map (\i ->
         reduce (+) 0.0 (map (\j -> signal[i + j] * kernel[k - 1i64 - j]) (iota k))
       ) (iota (n - k + 1i64))

def moving_average (arr: []f64) (window: i64) : []f64 =
  let n = length arr
  in if window <= 0i64 || window > n
     then []
     else
       map (\i ->
         reduce (+) 0.0 (map (\j -> arr[i + j]) (iota window)) / f64.i64 window
       ) (iota (n - window + 1i64))

def exponential_moving_average (arr: []f64) (alpha: f64) : []f64 =
  let n = length arr
  in if n == 0i64
     then []
     else
       let a =
         if alpha < 0.0 then 0.0
         else if alpha > 1.0 then 1.0
         else alpha
       let out0 = replicate n 0.0
       let out0 = out0 with [0] = arr[0]
       let (_, out) =
         loop (prev, acc) = (arr[0], out0) for i < n - 1i64 do
           let current = a * arr[i + 1i64] + (1.0 - a) * prev
           let acc = acc with [i + 1i64] = current
           in (current, acc)
       in out

def find_peaks (arr: []f64) (threshold: f64) : []i64 =
  let n = length arr
  in if n < 3i64
     then []
     else
       let candidates = map (\i -> i + 1i64) (iota (n - 2i64))
       in filter (\i -> arr[i] > arr[i - 1i64] && arr[i] > arr[i + 1i64] && arr[i] > threshold) candidates

entries.answer:
1. `find_max` is wrong on empty input because `reduce` yields the neutral element when there are no elements to combine, so this function returns `i64.lowest` instead of a real maximum.[1][2]

2. `find_min` has the same empty-input bug, returning `i64.highest` instead of signalling that no minimum exists.[2][1]

3. `mean_array` returns `0.0` for an empty array, which silently turns an undefined statistic into a valid-looking number and can corrupt later calculations.[2]

4. `variance_array` has the same empty-input defect, because variance of an empty dataset is undefined but the function returns `0.0` anyway.[2]

5. `std_dev_array` inherits that defect transitively, because it computes the square root of `variance_array arr` and therefore also reports `0.0` for empty input.[2]

6. `histogram` can overflow in `range = max_val - min_val` when the input spans extreme `i64` values, such as `i64.lowest` to `i64.highest`.[2]

7. `histogram` can also overflow in `range + num_bins - 1i64` before the division, so the computed bin size can become invalid even when `num_bins` itself is positive.[2]

8. `histogram` has a third overflow point in `(x - min_val) / bin_size`, because `x - min_val` can overflow for extreme negative `min_val`.[2]

9. `histogram` hides invalid input by returning `[]` when `num_bins <= 0i64`, which makes a bad parameter indistinguishable from a legitimate empty result.[2]

10. `scatter_array` silently truncates work to `min(length indices, length values)`, so any extra indices or values are dropped without error and data is lost.[2]

11. `scatter_array` silently ignores out-of-range indices instead of reporting them, which masks corrupted caller input.[2]

12. `scatter_array` resolves duplicate indices by last-write-wins because the loop updates the accumulator sequentially, so earlier writes to the same position are silently overwritten.[2]

13. `gather` silently substitutes `0i64` for every invalid index, which can fabricate data and make indexing bugs much harder to detect.[2]

14. `update_array` silently returns the original array when the index is invalid, so caller bugs are hidden instead of surfaced.[2]

15. `update_matrix` has the same masking behavior for both invalid row indices and invalid column indices, again returning the original matrix unchanged.[2]

16. `partition_array` is inefficient because it traverses the full array twice and allocates two filtered arrays, even though one pass is sufficient to build both partitions.[2]

17. `count_positive` allocates an unnecessary temporary array of `0/1` flags before reducing it, which is avoidable work and memory traffic.[1][2]

18. `any_positive` likewise materializes a full boolean array before reducing it, so it misses the natural early-exit behavior that this predicate-oriented operation should exploit.[1][2]

19. `all_positive` has the same avoidable temporary-allocation problem as `any_positive`.[1][2]

20. `all_equal` also builds a full mapped boolean array and then reduces it, doing more work than necessary for a property that can fail as soon as one mismatch is found.[1][2]

21. `sum_matrix` materializes an intermediate array of row sums and then reduces that array, instead of fusing the computation into a single pass.[1][2]

22. `matrix_multiply` uses the naive algorithm and additionally materializes `transpose b`, so it incurs substantial extra memory traffic and does not scale well for large matrices.[2]

23. `normalize_array` is inefficient because it computes the mean once directly and then computes it again indirectly through `std_dev_array -> variance_array -> mean_array`, causing an avoidable extra full pass over the input.[2]

24. `moving_average` is implemented as a naive sliding-window recomputation, so it does \(O(n \cdot window)\) work instead of using prefix sums to reduce the per-window cost.[1][2]

25. `convolve_1d` is also the naive direct implementation, so it repeats overlapping reads and does \(O(n \cdot k)\) work with no optimization for larger kernels.[2]

26. `exponential_moving_average` silently clamps invalid `alpha` values into `[0,1]` instead of rejecting them, which hides bad caller input and can make debugging parameter mistakes harder.[2]

27. `find_peaks` can never report a peak at index `0` or at the last index, so genuine endpoint peaks are systematically lost by construction.[2]

28. `cosine_similarity` returns `0.0` whenever either vector has zero magnitude, which conflates an undefined case with a valid orthogonal-similarity result.[2]

29. `softmax` contains an ineffective fallback branch `if sum_exp == 0.0` because, for ordinary finite non-empty input, subtracting the maximum guarantees at least one exponent of `1.0`, so the branch does not actually protect the bad numeric cases that matter, such as NaN contamination.[2]

30. `replicate_array` hides invalid negative lengths by returning `[]` instead of rejecting impossible size input.[2]

31. `iota_array` has the same problem, because negative lengths are silently mapped to `[]` rather than treated as an error in the caller’s logic.[2]

32. `prefix_sum` is semantically ambiguous because `scan` in Futhark is inclusive, so the function does not compute an exclusive prefix array that many readers will expect from that name.[1][2]
